name: Lattice Corneal Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Lattice Corneal Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic branching lattice-like amyloid deposits in the corneal stroma on slit-lamp examination
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the TGFBI gene
Histological confirmation of amyloid deposits in corneal biopsy specimens

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic lattice amyloid deposits on slit-lamp examination plus positive family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is increasingly used to confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and family history are definitive.

occasional.symptomName: Foreign body sensation in the eye

rare.symptomName: Corneal scarring leading to severe vision loss

laboratory: Histopathological identification of amyloid deposits with Congo red staining
Genetic testing revealing TGFBI gene mutations (e.g., R124C mutation)
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing branching lattice stromal opacities
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) demonstrating stromal deposits
genetic: Autosomal dominant mutations in TGFBI gene
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Discrete, crumb-like stromal opacities rather than branching lattice
Diffuse stromal haze with glycosaminoglycan deposits
Early onset stromal clouding without lattice pattern

redFlags: Recurrent, severe corneal erosions with pain
Signs of secondary infection or keratitis
references: Klintworth GK. Corneal dystrophies. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2009;4:7.
Weiss JS, Møller HU, Aldave AJ, et al. IC3D classification of corneal dystrophies—edition 2. Cornea. 2015;34(2):117-159.
Kaufman SC, et al. Corneal dystrophies: clinical and molecular genetics. Eye (Lond). 2017;31(1):1-15.
